column2: On the authority of Abū Mālik al-Ḥārith ibn ʿĀṣim al-Ashʿarī (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
“Purification is half of faith. Al-ḥamdu lillāh fills the Balance, and subḥān Allāh and al-ḥamdu lillāh fill—or: fills—what is between the heavens and the earth. Prayer is light, charity is proof,
patience is radiance, and the Qurʾān is an argument for you or against you. Every person goes out in the morning and sells himself, either freeing it or destroying it.” Reported by Muslim.
Al-ṭuhūr (“purification”): purifying oneself from ritual impurities; or what is meant is purity of the heart; or both together.
Shaṭr al-īmān (“half of faith”): half of faith. Al-mīzān (“the Balance”): that by which the deeds of [Allah's] servants are weighed. “Fills the Balance”: because of the greatness of its reward.
“Charity is proof”: evidence of its giver's faith.
“And the Qurʾān is an argument for you”: it guides you to salvation if you act on it; “or against you”: if you turn away from it.
Yaghdū (“goes out in the morning”): strives for himself. Fa-muʿtiquhā (“freeing it”): from punishment. Aw mūbiquhā (“or destroying it”): ruining it.
Affirmation of the Balance by which the deeds of the servants will be weighed on the Day of Resurrection.
The virtue of purification, and that it is half of faith.
The virtue of glorifying and praising [Allah].
The great reward of prayer, charity and patience.
Whoever acts on the Mighty Qurʾān, it leads him to Paradise; and whoever turns away from it and does not act on it is cast into the Fire.
Every person is striving either for his own destruction or for his own happiness.
This hadith guides us to the fact that whoever purifies his heart of doubts and corrupt beliefs, and purifies his body of ritual impurities, has taken hold of half of faith;

that whoever praises Allah the Exalted, the reward of his praise fills the Balance, and his glorifying and praising fill with reward what is between the heaven and the earth, because the one who praises Allah extols his Lord, Glorified is He, with every kind of praise,
including the attributes of perfection and majesty that belong to Allah, while the one who glorifies Him declares Allah free of deficiencies, faults and defects;

that prayer is a light by which a person is guided now and later, just as charity is evidence and proof of the strength of its giver's faith; and that the servant's patience in obeying Allah and in the trials and hardships that befall him is a cause of increase in the light of his insight.
So he is patient with what Allah [has decreed] for him, because he believes in that. Everyone strives for himself:
among them is one who sells himself to Allah by obeying Him, and so frees himself from the Fire on the Day of Resurrection;

and among people is one who sells himself to the devil and the whims of his soul, and so destroys himself on the Day of Resurrection, and the punishment may even be hastened for him in this world. We ask Allah for well-being.
Among what has been said on this:
Whoever sows evil reaps from its consequences / regret, and for the reaping of the crop there is a season.
Another poet:
A man has no home after death to dwell in / except the one he builds before death.
If he builds it with good, his dwelling is pleasant; / if he builds it with evil, its builder has failed.
So plant the roots of piety while you are able to strive, / and know that after death you will meet them.
